# Isolde Pembroke

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c19 P85](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0085), [v2 c26 P45](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0045)</sub>

## Appearance

By the time she reaches forty-five, Isolde anticipates she will be terribly stout.

_Sources: [v2 c26 P56](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0056)_

## Personality

Isolde is an affectionate and sensitive young woman who is deeply attached to her friends. She is far less capable of bearing people's anger than Nell is and easily feels apprehensive when facing scolding. Though she occasionally doubts her own intelligence compared to others, she possesses a warm sense of humor and enjoys shared games, dares, and playful fun.

_Sources: [v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052), [v1 c19 P87](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0087), [v1 c19 P90](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0090), [v2 c26 P45](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0045)_

## Traits

- fear of living as an old maid  <sub>[v2 c26 P56](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0056)</sub>
- sensitive to scolding

## Abilities

- solo singing  <sub>[v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014)</sub>
- acting in school dialogues

## History

While attending Brierley School under Miss Thorne, Isolde rehearsed school dialogues such as 'A Morning Visit' alongside Opal Pettigrew and Odette Pullen, and performed a solo song in a student concert. She became best friends with Nell Harcourt, exchanging notes and gifts like red tissue paper bookmarks across the school grounds. During a sleepover at her house, she and Nell accidentally leaped onto a bed occupied by her visiting relative, Aunt Lavinia Pembroke, startling her and causing a stir. Isolde later attended Regent's and subsequently moved on to attend Wexcombe College with Nell. While discussing suitors and future prospects with Nell, she expressed her anxieties about growing older and remaining unmarried.

_Sources: [v1 c17 P30](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0030), [v1 c17 P32](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0032), [v1 c19 P48](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0048), [v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052), [v1 c19 P54](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0054), [v1 c19 P60](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0060), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v2 c26 P45](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0045), [v2 c26 P56](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0056), [v2 c26 P58](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0058)_
